summary: Early on, a newcomer's brief, specific questions are treated as normal, not a bother.
realLife: Onboarding advice says clarifying tasks is good practice for newcomers and that requests should be short and specific, such as asking for a couple of minutes.
sources: Atlassian Work Life, starting a new job and first week success: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/teamwork/starting-a-new-job-and-first-week-success
inGame: Voice of the new-coworker event: a newcomer with a curious or careful trait asking how things run, tied to the job record (employer, position, workplace, pay, tenure) in the jobs module.

turns.summary: The manager sighs at each question and the newcomer stops asking.
turns.writesBack: The newcomer's mood dips and mistakes follow later.

turns.summary: The newcomer holds questions back for fear of looking slow.
turns.writesBack: A mistake is made later, and a note is made in the journal.

turns.summary: The newcomer asks so many questions that coworkers get tired of answering.
turns.writesBack: Coworker ties cool and the manager offers a fixed hour for questions.
